The shop states it uses 本わらび粉 — real bracken starch, not the potato-starch substitute most shops use — and warabimochi dressed with kinako and kuromitsu is starch, roasted soy flour and sugar syrup with no wheat and no animal product in it at all. tokyo_aburi_miso_ramen_mensho_.price_note: SAMURAI NOODLE PUBLISHES ITS FULL MENU IN JAPANESE AND ENGLISH AND PRINTS NO PRICES AT ALL — every line ends in a row of leader dots with the figure omitted, in both languages, and the card closes 「価格は店舗によって異なる場合があります。各店舗のメニューをご確認ください」. So the item list below is authoritative and the prices are simply not published; do not treat the blanks as unresearched. The company's head office is 渋谷区道玄坂2-10-3, the same street as this branch. ⚠ THIS IS ONE OF THE MOST IMPORTANT GLUTEN-FREE ADDRESSES IN THE TOKYO SET AND IT SHOULD BE TREATED AS A PRIORITY FOR PRICE CONFIRMATION. The shop runs a dedicated グルテンフリー section of four bowls — GF味噌, GF辛味噌, GF醤油, GF塩 — plus a ヴィーガン/ベジタリアン section of five, and the two sections overlap in one line, グルテンフリー ヴィーガンラーメン, which is the single dish that satisfies both. The side menu carries GFヴィーガン餃子, GF唐揚げ and GFフライドポテト: a gluten-free gyoza and a gluten-free kara-age are both things that essentially do not exist in ordinary Japanese ramen shops, and a fried item labelled GF implies a fryer the shop is willing to vouch for. ⚠ WHAT THE SHOP DOES NOT PUBLISH IS AS IMPORTANT AS WHAT IT DOES. There is no allergen table, no statement about separate pots or separate fryers, and no ingredient list for the GF tare — and a GF SOY-SAUCE ramen necessarily means a tamari or a wheat-free shoyu that the shop has not named. Everything in the GF section is recorded gf on the strength of the shop's own explicit label and nothing more; the cross-contact question is exactly the one to ask at the counter. ⚠ THE VEGAN BOWLS ARE NOT GLUTEN-FREE unless they are the one line that says so: ヴィーガン味噌, ヴィーガン辛味噌 and ヴィーガン醤油 are vegan ramen on ordinary wheat noodles. オリエンタルベジタリアンラーメン is the Buddhist-style no-alliums bowl and is recorded vegan-ask because oriental vegetarian excludes the five pungent roots but does not by itself exclude egg or dairy.

The lunch PDF (1.9 MB) extracts to two bytes — it is an image scan. The dinner PDF (8.9 MB) does extract, but only the English item names: every Japanese string and every price is set in an embedded Adobe-Japan1 CID font that pdftotext cannot map, so the numbers come out as separator glyphs. That is a finding, not a failure — the English dish names below are read from that PDF and are real, but their prices genuinely could not be read from the file. The two priced lines recorded here are the shop's own limited-period campaign images, whose alt text carries the figures: 担仔乾麺セット 850円（税込）and 麻辣湯セット 1,100円（税込）, both marked 【期間限定サービス価格】台南担仔麵水道橋店のみ販売. Also first-party: 宴会 courses with nomihodai from 3,980円, 70 seats, closed Sundays, and the group is シンガポール海南鶏飯グループ. ⚠ THE MOST USEFUL THING ON THIS MENU FOR A COELIAC IS THE 米粉 AND THE RICE. 台湾式焼きビーフン is rice vermicelli and 魯肉飯 and 排骨飯 are rice plates — but 魯肉飯 is braised in soy by definition, the shop itself describes the 担仔麺's traditional topping as 魯蛋、「醤油味のゆで卵」, and 排骨 is a battered fried cutlet. Two independent public resolvers — Google 8.8.8.8 and Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 — both return SERVFAIL for the domain, which means the zone's own nameservers are not answering (or the zone is failing DNSSEC validation), not that the name has been withdrawn the way an NXDOMAIN would say. Either way there is no page to fetch from this machine today and no menu has been read. This is distinct from the 渋谷更科 case, where the name is genuinely gone: a SERVFAIL can clear on its own, so this record is worth one cheap retry on a future tick rather than a rewrite. The dataset's only other link is Tabelog, which serves a Cloudflare managed challenge to this egress. Treat the two records as siblings, not duplicates: the addresses, phone numbers and prices differ, and 菩提樹 carries a wagyu-steak and hamburg range the tonkatsu shop does not. ⚠ THE MOST USEFUL SINGLE FINDING IS THE SAUCE CHOICE ON THE HEADLINE DISH, AND IT IS BAD NEWS. The A5 wagyu hamburg — the shop's signature, ground in-house — offers exactly three sauces: デミグラスソース, ガーリックオイル醤油 and わさび醤油. Demi-glace is a wheat roux and the other two are soy sauce, so the shop's flagship dish has no wheat-free dressing on offer. Sets come with rice or 青しそご飯, 八丁味噌の赤出汁, salad and pickles — Hatcho miso is a pure soybean miso with no barley, which is a genuine point in its favour, but the dashi under it is bonito. ⚠ Nothing on this card is vegan; 揚げ出し豆腐 and もずく酢 are the only two plant-centred dishes and both are dashi-and-soy dressed.

tokyo_rami_chan_no_daidokoro_r.price_note: Prices 税込, from the shop's own HotPepper page (千代田区神田三崎町2-12-5 ニュー千代田ビル — the record's Suidobashi/Kanda-Misakicho placement), which trades as 「スパイス×焼き鳥居酒屋 ラミちゃんの台所水道橋店」. ⚠ THE RECORD CALLS THIS NEPALESE AND THAT UNDERSELLS HOW ODD AND HOW USEFUL THE CARD IS: it is a Nepalese kitchen running a Japanese yakitori counter, so a spice-forward Nepali section (モモ, チョイラ, ニャパー, タンドール oven work) sits beside conventional 焼鳥 at ¥90–160 a skewer. That combination is why several genuinely wheat-free-leaning dishes exist here that you would not find in either cuisine alone. ⚠ THE BEST FINDINGS ARE THE TANDOOR AND THE PAPPADUM. タンドリーチキン is yoghurt-and-spice marinated and baked in the clay oven with no flour step, チキンティッカ and シークケバブ likewise, and マサラパパッド at ¥100 is stated by the shop to be 「豆粉を捏ねて薄く伸ばして焼いたせんべい」 — a LENTIL-FLOUR cracker, which is a rare genuinely non-wheat snack on a Tokyo izakaya card. ⚠ THE MOMO ARE THE TRAP THAT LOOKS LIKE A WIN: 蒸しモモ is a steamed dumpling, and momo wrappers are WHEAT. スープモモ likewise. ⚠ 生春巻 is stated by the shop to be wrapped in ライスペーパー — rice paper, not wheat — and is orderable with or without prawn and avocado (+¥100). ⚠ ネパール風焼きそば and ネパール風ラーメン are wheat noodles; パッタイ is stated by the shop to be a RICE noodle (「ライスヌードルを使った」). tokyo_gyossantei_shibuya.price_note: ⚠ EVERY PRICE HERE IS HISTORICAL AND THE PAGE SAYS SO. The shop’s only website on file is a Facebook page, and Facebook returned HTTP 400 to this egress, so the shop publishes nothing readable of its own. Hot Pepper is the only itemised menu that could be read, and it stamps its own pages: 料理 2015/08/25 更新, ランチ 2015/08/25 更新, ドリンク 2015/08/25 更新, テイクアウト 2020/05/18 更新 — and prints the warning ※更新日が2021/3/31以前の情報は、当時の価格及び税率に基づく情報となります. The 2015 prices therefore predate the October 2019 rise to 10% consumption tax entirely. Treat them as a shape, not a bill. Retty’s menu page was also read: it lists dish names under 料理/ランチ/ドリンク but carries no prices at all, so it adds nothing. Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THE DIETARY SHAPE OF A MIYAZAKI HOUSE, WHICH IS NOT WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE: the two dishes this shop is known for are both closed to a coeliac and both closed to a plant-eater, for different reasons. チキン南蛮 is chicken floured, egged and fried, then finished in a sweet vinegar-soy sauce — wheat in the coating and wheat again in the soy. 冷汁 is a cold miso soup poured over rice, and Miyazaki’s version is built on grilled fish; the miso itself is commonly 麦味噌, barley miso, which Japanese labelling law does not require anyone to declare. The one dish on the list a vegetarian would reach for, がんもの揚げだし, is a tofu fritter sitting in dashi-and-soy broth, so it fails on the liquid rather than the solid. The shop publishes no allergen chart anywhere.

items.note: 角煮の煮汁は醤油・味醂・砂糖＝小麦。The braising liquor is soy sauce, which is wheat, and it is the medium the meat cooks in rather than a sauce on the side. Pork.

items.en: Hiyajiru — Miyazaki’s cold miso soup, poured over rice and eaten in summer. Hot Pepper prints no price for this one
items.price: お問い合わせください (price not published — ask)
items.section: 料理 A la carte (2015/08/25 更新)
items.note: 宮崎の冷汁は焼き魚（主に鯵）と味噌が基本。麦味噌の場合、麦＝大麦は日本の表示義務対象外。Miyazaki hiyajiru is built on grilled fish worked into miso with sesame, so a bowl that arrives looking like vegetables over rice is a fish dish. The miso is the gluten question: barley miso (麦味噌) is the regional norm and barley is NOT on Japan’s statutory allergen list, so nobody has to tell you. The shop publishes no ingredient list. Ask before ordering, and expect the answer to be fish.

items.en: Agedashi ganmodoki — a deep-fried tofu-and-vegetable dumpling sitting in warm broth
items.section: 料理 A la carte (2015/08/25 更新)
items.note: THIS IS THE ITEM A VEGETARIAN WILL POINT AT, AND IT IS THE TRAP. がんも自体は豆腐と野菜だが、揚げだしの出汁は鰹だし＋醤油。The fritter is plant food; the broth it arrives in is bonito dashi seasoned with soy sauce, so the animal content and the wheat are both in the liquid, not the thing you were looking at. Ganmodoki is also commonly bound with grated yam or egg white, which the shop does not declare.

items.en: Chicken nanban set, lunch only — the fried chicken with rice, soup and pickles
items.note: Same battered, soy-sauced chicken as the a la carte plate. A 定食 adds miso soup, which at a Japanese lunch counter is dashi-based, so the set is further from vegan than the plate, not closer.

items.en: Hiyajiru set, lunch only — the cold miso soup with rice and sides
items.note: See 冷汁 above: grilled fish worked into miso, and the miso is very likely barley. The set format does not change either fact.

items.en: Chicken nanban bento to take away — the cheapest route to the shop’s signature dish
items.section: テイクアウト Takeaway (2020/05/18 更新)
items.note: Tax-inclusive and the most recently updated price on the whole Hot Pepper listing, so the closest thing here to a current figure. Same wheat batter and soy-vinegar sauce.

items.ja: ちきん南蛮定食（テイクアウト）
items.en: Chicken nanban set, boxed to take away
items.section: テイクアウト Takeaway (2020/05/18 更新)
items.note: Wheat batter, soy-based sweet vinegar sauce, egg tartare. Chicken.

items.en: The house set — the shop’s own name on a box, contents not published
items.section: テイクアウト Takeaway (2020/05/18 更新)
items.note: Hot Pepper lists the name and the price and nothing else. Do not assume: a house teishoku at a Miyazaki izakaya could be the chicken, the fish or both. Ask what is in it before ordering, and assume the miso soup is dashi-based unless told otherwise.

items.ja: 冷汁定食（テイクアウト）
items.en: Hiyajiru set, boxed
items.section: テイクアウト Takeaway (2020/05/18 更新)
items.note: Cold soup travels, which is why this one is on the takeaway list. Still grilled fish and miso.

items.en: Aya set — named for Aya, the Miyazaki town known nationally for its organic farming; contents not published
items.section: テイクアウト Takeaway (2020/05/18 更新)
items.note: The shop’s own Hot Pepper blurb elsewhere mentions 綾町直送有機野菜の温サラダ, warm salad of organic vegetables sent direct from Aya, so the name points at vegetables — but no composition is published for this box and a Japanese teishoku almost always includes a dashi-based soup. Worth asking about specifically if you want the vegetable-forward option; do not assume it is meat-free.

items.en: Hideji Beer on draught — the Miyazaki craft brewery, poured here as the regional beer to go with the regional food
items.section: ドリンク Drinks (2015/08/25 更新)
items.note: ビールは大麦麦芽＝グルテン。Beer is barley malt; there is no gluten-free option on this list.

items.en: Shochu, various — the drink Miyazaki is actually famous for; the list itself is not published
items.section: ドリンク Drinks (2015/08/25 更新)
items.note: 各種＝銘柄未掲載。麦焼酎は九州の定番で、麦＝大麦。“Various” is doing a lot of work here: Kyushu shochu is distilled from sweet potato (芋), barley (麦), rice (米) or buckwheat, and barley shochu is one of the commonest styles in the region. Distillation removes gluten protein in practice, but if you avoid barley on principle, ask which base before you order. Plant-based either way.

tokyo_kayuya_sato_kayu_ya_sato.price_note: ⚠ THE DASHI IS THE WHOLE STORY AND IT IS NOT VEGETARIAN. This is a Taiwanese-congee specialist behind Sensō-ji, and a bowl of rice porridge with vegetables on it is exactly the dish a plant-eater assumes is safe. It is not: Rurubu, quoting the shop, states 「魯肉粥」のだしは干しシイタケと干しエビ — the base is reconstituted DRIED SHIITAKE AND DRIED SHRIMP. Popeye, reporting the same kitchen, gives the provenance as 島根県産の干し椎茸と干し海老の戻し汁で炊いている, cooked in the soaking liquid of Shimane dried shiitake and dried shrimp. The shrimp is in the cooking water, so it cannot be left off, and it is a crustacean — one of Japan’s eight statutory allergens — hiding inside what reads as a mushroom porridge. The other published bowl, 鶏レモン粥, is 鶏だしと昆布だしで炊いた粥, chicken and kelp. Neither published porridge is meat-free, and the shop publishes no vegetarian one. ⚠ WHEAT: the 蒸籠 that upgrades an A set to a B set contains 手包み鶏シウマイ — hand-wrapped chicken shumai, and a shumai wrapper is wheat. 魯肉 is pork braised in soy sauce, wheat again. The steamed vegetables in the same basket (about six seasonal kinds, from the Chiba grower キレドベジタブルアトリエ) are the one genuinely plant part of the meal and they share the basket with the shumai. ⚠ PRICING SHAPE: the sets are quoted as ranges because the price moves with which porridge you choose — Aセット 1,200円〜 (porridge plus two small dishes), Bセット 1,650円〜 (porridge, two small dishes, the steamer basket and annin tofu). Rurubu names two worked examples at B-set level. Roughly five porridges are on at any time including seasonal ones; only these two are published. Instagram is the shop’s only channel and serves a login wall to this egress; Tabelog has served HTTP 403 to this egress since 2026-09-02.

items.en: Set A — your choice of congee with two small side dishes. The base set; the price moves with which congee you pick
items.note: お粥のだしは干し椎茸＋干し海老、または鶏だし＋昆布だし。The porridge choice decides everything, and both published choices contain animal: dried shrimp in one, chicken in the other. Gluten depends on the small dishes and on the porridge’s seasoning, neither published in full — a Taiwanese congee house seasons with soy sauce as a matter of course.

items.en: Set B — congee, two small dishes, a bamboo steamer of vegetables and shumai, and annin tofu to finish
items.note: The steamer is what makes this the bigger set, and the steamer is what closes it: 手包み鶏シウマイ 2個, two hand-wrapped chicken shumai, whose wrapper is wheat, sharing the basket with the vegetables. Not gluten-free at any porridge choice.

items.en: Lu rou congee as a B set — the Taiwanese braised-pork porridge the owner built after eating at 三娘香菇肉粥 in Taipei and reverse-engineering it
items.note: ⚠ だしは干しシイタケと干しエビ＝甲殻類。The base broth is dried shiitake AND DRIED SHRIMP — crustacean, in the cooking liquid, unremovable. On top of that 魯肉 is pork braised in soy sauce, so wheat as well. This is the shop’s signature and it is closed to a vegetarian, a shellfish allergy and a coeliac alike.

items.en: Chicken and lemon congee as a B set — cooked in chicken stock and kombu rather than the shrimp base
items.note: 鶏だしと昆布だしで炊いた粥。Chicken stock plus kelp. No dried shrimp in this one, which matters if the shellfish rather than the meat is your problem. Chicken, so not vegetarian. Gluten unpublished; assume soy seasoning unless the counter says otherwise.

items.en: Simmered egg, as a topping on any porridge
items.note: 煮玉子＝醤油ダレで煮る＝小麦。A simmered egg is simmered in soy, so a plain-looking egg is a wheat item. Egg.

items.en: Additive-free pickled plum — the shop specifies 無添加, nothing added
items.note: 無添加の梅干しは梅・塩・赤紫蘇のみが基本。A genuinely additive-free umeboshi is plum, salt and red shiso and nothing else, which makes this the cleanest thing on the list — but it is going into a porridge whose base is shrimp or chicken, so it does not rescue the bowl. Kept at ask for gluten because the shop publishes no ingredient statement.

items.en: First-harvest nori — the tender early-season cut, torn over the porridge
items.note: 焼海苔なら海藻のみだが、味付海苔は醤油。Plain toasted nori is seaweed alone; seasoned nori (味付海苔) is glazed with soy sauce, and shops rarely say which they buy. Nori is also farmed in waters where shrimp and crab occur, which some Japanese allergen charts declare.

items.ja: 鹹豆漿（シェントウジャン）
items.en: Shentoujiang — savoury warm soy milk, curdled with vinegar until it sets into loose curds. The Taiwanese breakfast dish, served here from the 9am opening
items.note: 鹹豆漿は豆乳を酢で固めたもの。台湾では油條（小麦の揚げパン）、干し海老、菜脯を載せるのが定番。The soy milk base itself is plant and wheat-free, which is why this looks like the vegan-and-coeliac answer on the list. Taiwanese practice loads the bowl with a torn youtiao — a deep-fried WHEAT dough stick — and commonly dried shrimp and preserved radish as well. This shop, whose congee base is dried shrimp, publishes no ingredient list for this bowl. Ask what goes on top before assuming.

items.ja: 蒸籠（手包み鶏シウマイ＋季節の蒸し野菜）
items.romaji: seiro (te-tsutsumi tori shūmai + kisetsu no mushi-yasai)
items.en: The bamboo steamer that comes with a B set — two hand-wrapped chicken shumai and around six seasonal steamed vegetables sent from the Chiba grower Kiredo Vegetable Atelier
items.price: Bセットに含む (included in Set B; not sold separately at a published price)
items.note: シウマイの皮＝小麦、餡は鶏。The vegetables are the good part and they are genuinely good — a named single-farm supplier, about six kinds, changing with the season. They are steamed in the same basket as two chicken shumai whose wrappers are wheat. If you need either restriction respected, this basket has to be discussed at the counter, not assumed.

items.en: Annin tofu — the almond-milk pudding that closes a B set
items.price: Bセットに含む (included in Set B)
items.note: 杏仁豆腐は牛乳・生クリームで作るのが一般的で、ゼラチンを使う店もある。Standard annin tofu is set with milk or cream, and some kitchens use gelatine rather than agar — either would make it neither vegan nor vegetarian. The shop publishes no recipe. Ask.

tokyo_asakusa_hatoya_vegan_fru.price_note: ⚠ A COMPLETELY VEGAN SHOP THAT IS COMPLETELY CLOSED TO A COELIAC, AND THAT IS THE ONLY THING WORTH KNOWING HERE. Japan VegeMap lists this shop under すべてVEGAN（完全菜食）/ all-vegan, and Hachidory lists it in the same category; VegeMap’s own description is “Large pieces of fresh fruit in vegan cream, sandwiched between fluffy white bread.” So the cream is a plant cream and the whole counter is animal-free — an unusually clean answer for a takeaway you eat walking around Asakusa. The bread is the problem: a fruit sando IS white shokupan, and shokupan is wheat. There is no rice-flour version and none is advertised. A gluten-free traveller reading “vegan fruit sandwich specialist” should read “nothing here”. ⚠ The shop publishes nothing itself beyond Instagram, which serves a login wall to this egress, so the prices below come from directory listings rather than the shop’s own board: VegeMap gives a 600 yen floor for the fruit sandwich generally, Hachidory names kiwi and strawberry at 700 yen each, and Yahoo! Map carries a user-submitted strawberry sandwich at 700 yen — the two independent 700 figures agree, which is why this is recorded at medium rather than low. Neither source states what the vegan cream is actually made from (soy, coconut, oat and cashew are all common in this niche); if you are avoiding a specific plant allergen rather than animal products, that still has to be asked at the counter. Tabelog has served HTTP 403 to this egress since 2026-09-02.

items.ja: フルーツサンド（いちご・キウイ・オレンジ・季節のフルーツ）
items.en: The fruit sandwich, in whichever fruit is on that day — strawberry, kiwi, orange and seasonal others. Big pieces of fruit set in plant cream between soft white bread
items.section: ヴィーガンフルーツサンド Vegan fruit sandwiches
items.note: 完全菜食の店。クリームは植物性。ただしパンは食パン＝小麦。Animal-free throughout — the shop is listed as すべてVEGAN by Japan VegeMap and the cream is described as vegan cream. The bread is ordinary white shokupan, which is wheat, and it is the majority of the sandwich. No gluten-free bread is offered.

items.en: Strawberry sandwich — the one everybody photographs, halved so the fruit shows in cross-section
items.section: ヴィーガンフルーツサンド Vegan fruit sandwiches
items.note: Plant cream, no dairy, no egg — genuinely vegan. Wheat bread, so genuinely not gluten-free. Both facts are firm; what the cream is based on is not published, so a soy or nut allergy still needs a question.

items.en: Kiwi sandwich — same build, green cross-section
items.section: ヴィーガンフルーツサンド Vegan fruit sandwiches
items.note: Same plant cream and same wheat shokupan as the strawberry. Kiwi is itself a declared allergen in some jurisdictions though not one of Japan’s eight statutory ones.

tokyo_shojin_ramen_sai.price_note: ⚠ THE RAMEN PRICES ARE NOT PUBLISHED ANYWHERE THIS MACHINE CAN READ, AND THAT IS WHY THIS RECORD IS SHORT. The shop opened in Shibuya in April 2026 and its only channel is Instagram, which serves a login wall to this egress. Hot Pepper carries the shop but shows no itemised menu on either its main page or its コース page (its budget band is 2001〜3000円 at both lunch and dinner). Gnavi carries only the opening announcement and a discounted ゆず塩ラーメン promotion with no standing price. Tabelog has served HTTP 403 to this egress since 2026-09-02. The two items below are the only priced dishes on any page that could actually be read: they come from a press release issued by Agro Ludens, the company that supplies the shop’s protein, which names them and their tax-inclusive prices outright. ⚠ WHAT IS GENUINELY ESTABLISHED, AND IT IS THE USEFUL PART: the release describes the shop as serving 動物性食材を使用しない「精進ラーメン」 — shojin ramen using no animal ingredients at all — at 東京都渋谷区宇田川町11-2, opened 2026年4月. Hot Pepper’s own subtitle is ヴィーガンラーメン and a customer review there records 動物性や魚介を使っていないと聞いていた. So the animal-free claim is corroborated from two directions. ⚠ AND THE PART A COELIAC MUST NOT MISREAD: the release states the new protein, 米由来マイコプロテイン Comeat®, is 麹菌を用いて、国産米のタンパク質を発酵させてつくった and is 高タンパク質・低脂質であることに加え、グルテンフリーかつ主要アレルゲンフリー — the PROTEIN is gluten-free and free of the major allergens. That says nothing whatever about the bowls. This is a ramen shop; a ramen noodle is wheat unless a shop says otherwise, and this one says nothing about its noodle, its tare or its miso. A gluten-free ingredient inside a wheat bowl is still a wheat bowl. Vegan travellers can eat here with confidence; coeliacs cannot, on anything published so far.

items.en: Mini “meat” miso rice bowl — a small donburi of savoury miso-cooked protein over rice, added to the menu alongside the ramen. The “meat” is Comeat®, a mycoprotein grown by fermenting the protein of Japanese-grown rice with koji mould
items.note: 動物性食材不使用の店。Comeat®自体はグルテンフリー表示だが、肉味噌の味噌・調味料の表示なし。Vegan with confidence — the shop uses no animal ingredients and the protein is fermented rice, not soy meat and not gluten seitan, which is unusual and worth knowing if you avoid both. Gluten is the open question: the protein is declared gluten-free, but 肉味噌 is protein cooked down in miso and seasonings, and neither the miso (which may be 麦味噌, barley) nor the rest of the seasoning is declared. Ask.

items.en: The same bowl finished with mayonnaise — plant-based, since the kitchen uses no animal products
items.note: Egg-free mayonnaise by implication of the shop’s no-animal-ingredients policy. Same unanswered question about the miso as the plain version.
